sentences.text:
Author: Surepalli Nanda
Bench: Surepalli Nanda
 Hon'Ble Mrs Justice Surepalli Nanda
 Writ Petition No.18861 of 2023
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Irrigation and Command Area Development appearing for respondent No.1, learned Government Pleader for Finance and Planning Department appearing for respondent No.2 and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.3 to 5.
2.

The grievance of the petitioners in this writ petition is that in spite of passing a common judgment and decree, dated 26.09.2013 in L.A.A.S.Nos.925, 933, 934, 936 and 946 of 2011 by this Court and the petitioners filing E.P.Nos.3 of 2021, 4 of 2022, 5 of 2022, 2 of 2021 and 3 of 2022 on the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge, Wanaparthy, the judgement debtor i.e.., respondent No.5 failed to deposit the decretal amount even after lapse of more than eight years and the said E.P is being adjourned from time to time.
WP_18861_2023 SN,J 3.

The facts of the case are that the land in Survey No.306/2 situated at Janampet Village, was acquired by Land Acquisition officer, by passing an Award, dated 15.09.1999 and on the request made by the petitioners herein, the same was referred to the Court of Senior Civil Judge,
Wanaparthy under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act, 1894').
By its Judgment and decree dated 26.10.2004 the competent Civil Court dismissed the reference confirming the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

Aggrieved by the same,
L.A.A.S.Nos.925, 933, 934, 936 and 946 of 2011 dated 26.09.2013 were preferred before this Court and this Court allowed the appeals by fixing the compensation at Rs.65,000/- per acre for dry lands and Rs.75,000/- per acre for irrigated dry/wet lands.

Seeking execution of the said judgment and decree as modified, the petitioners herein filed E.P.Nos.3 of 2021, 4 of 2022, 5 of 2022, 2 of 2021 and 3 of 2022 on the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge, Wanaparthy.

entities.text: Court of Senior Civil Judge, Wanaparthy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the said E.P., respondent No.5 herein stated to have entered appearance and the said execution proceedings are being dragged on from time to time and are still pending.
Respondent No.5 herein failed to deposit WP_18861_2023 SN,J the decretal amount in spite of the said judgment and decree having become final.

Aggrieved by the said inaction on the part of respondent No.5 and the action of respondent Nos.1 and 2 in making available the required funds for complying with the said judgment and decree, the present writ petition is filed.

sentences.text:
4. Having, taken note of the facts and circumstances of the case, especially, the fact that the property of the petitioners was acquired, as early as, in the year 1999 and they are deprived of their property without fixing the proper compensation and though proper compensation was fixed by this Court as early as on 26.09.2013, the petitioners are not being paid with said compensation as of date i.e.,
even after lapse of more than eight years, and in the light of law laid down by this Court in the case of Bhamidipati Annaporna Bhavani v. Land Acquisition Officer1 holding that the writ petition is maintainable even when execution proceedings are pending seeking a direction for payment of compensation as fixed by the reference Court

entities.text: Bhamidipati Annaporna Bhavani v. Land Acquisition Officer1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , this Court is left with no other option except to declare that the action on the part of the (2005 (3) ALD 233) WP_18861_2023 SN,J respondents is totally arbitrary, illegal and violative of Article 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India.

5. In the circumstances, the Writ Petition is allowed directing the respondents to deposit the entire decretal amount covered by common judgment and decree in L.A.A.S.Nos.925, 933, 934, 936 and 946 of 2011 dated 26.09.2013 into the credit of the E.P.Nos.3 of 2021, 4 of 2022, 5 of 2022, 2 of 2021 and 3 of 2022
on the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge, Wanaparthy,
within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order

. 
6. It is made clear that any negligence on the part of the respondents in complying with this order within the time stipulated will be viewed seriously and in such an event, the respondents would be liable to pay heavy costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.

MRS JUSTICE SUREPALLI NANDA Date:
19.07.2023 Kgk T. Thirupathaiah vs The State Of Telangana on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177619893/
